Class OidcProviderUtils

java.lang.Object
iu.oidc.provider.OidcProviderUtils
final class OidcProviderUtils extends Object
Request-shaping logic shared by this provider's endpoints.

Every endpoint reads scope the same way, matches a redirect_uri against a client's registrations the same way, and resolves what resource a request may act on the same way. Holding that here once, rather than duplicated or reached into across endpoints, is what keeps them from drifting apart on it.

Nothing here writes a response. Building an error redirect is here because the shape of one is OAuth 2.0's; sending it is the caller's.

    • isValidResource

      static boolean isValidResource(String resource)
      Determines whether a resource parameter value is well-formed.

      RFC 8707 §2 requires an absolute URI with no fragment component; a value that isn't one names no target this provider could ever issue a token for.

      Parameters:
      resource - value to check
      Returns:
      true if resource is an absolute URI with no fragment; else false
      See Also:
      • RFC 8707 §2

    • isRegisteredResource

      static boolean isRegisteredResource(edu.iu.oidc.config.IuOidcClientEndpoint endpoint, URI issuer, String resource)
      Determines whether an endpoint registers a resource entry naming the given URI.

      An entry with no URI names this provider's own issuer identifier rather than an external resource, so a request naming the issuer itself matches it the same as one naming an external resource matches an entry registered for that URI.

      Parameters:
      endpoint - verified client endpoint
      issuer - this provider's issuer identifier
      resource - resource URI, as a string
      Returns:
      true if the endpoint registers an entry naming that URI; else false

    • resourcesGrantingScope

      static Set<String> resourcesGrantingScope(edu.iu.oidc.config.IuOidcClientEndpoint endpoint, URI issuer, Set<String> scopes)
      Infers which resources a request naming no resource parameter should be understood to act on, from the scope it asks for.

      Naming no resource doesn't restrict a request to just the entry registered without a URI: every resource whose scope overlaps what was requested is included. That is what lets a client ask for an external resource's scope without also having to name that resource explicitly.

      Parameters:
      endpoint - verified client endpoint
      issuer - this provider's issuer identifier
      scopes - requested scopes
      Returns:
      resource URIs whose registered scope overlaps a requested one; empty if none do

    • grantedResources

      static Set<edu.iu.oidc.config.IuOidcClientResource> grantedResources(edu.iu.oidc.config.IuOidcClientEndpoint endpoint, URI issuer, Set<String> resources)
      Determines the resources a request through one endpoint may act on.

      An endpoint's resources are filtered by the requested resource values, so a client registered for several resources only gets the scopes of the ones it named. A request naming none matches the resource registered without a URI, which is how a client that acts on only one resource registers it — that same entry also names this provider's own issuer identifier rather than an external resource, so a request that names the issuer explicitly matches it too. A matching entry that grants no scope contributes nothing and is left out, the same as one that doesn't match at all.

      openid is not a special case: a client that wants an ID token issued registers a resource whose scope includes openid the same as any other.

      Parameters:
      endpoint - verified client endpoint
      issuer - this provider's issuer identifier
      resources - resource parameter values; empty if the request named none
      Returns:
      resources granting at least one scope the request may ask for; empty if the endpoint registers none matching

    • registeredEndpoint

      static edu.iu.oidc.config.IuOidcClientEndpoint registeredEndpoint(edu.iu.oidc.config.IuOidcClientConfiguration client, String redirectUri)
      Matches a requested redirect URI against the client's registered endpoints.

      OpenID Connect requires an exact comparison, so a URI that merely starts with a registered value doesn't match.

      Parameters:
      client - client configuration
      redirectUri - redirect_uri parameter value
      Returns:
      registered endpoint, or null if the parameter is missing or names no registered endpoint

    • audience

      static Set<URI> audience(URI issuer, edu.iu.oidc.config.IuOidcClientEndpoint endpoint, Set<String> resources, Set<String> scopes)
      Names the audience an access token issued to an endpoint is addressed to.

      Derived from the resources the endpoint registers whose scope is among those granted, so a token scoped to one resource isn't also addressed to another the request never asked for. A resource with no URI names this provider's own issuer identifier rather than an external resource — that entry is what a request naming no resource matches, so registering it with a granted scope such as openid is how a deployment explicitly addresses a token to itself, without embedding its own issuer URI in the registration to do it.

      Nothing is added when nothing matches: an endpoint that registers no resource for a granted scope hasn't said what that scope's token should be addressed to, and answering with this provider's issuer anyway would grant an audience nobody configured.

      Parameters:
      issuer - this provider's issuer identifier
      endpoint - endpoint that authenticated
      resources - resources the token is addressed to; empty to consider every one of the endpoint's resources whose scope was granted
      scopes - granted scopes
      Returns:
      audience URIs; empty if the endpoint registers no resource for any granted scope

    • clientCredentialsScopes

      static Set<String> clientCredentialsScopes(edu.iu.oidc.config.IuOidcClientEndpoint endpoint, URI issuer, String scope, Set<String> resources)
      Determines the scope a client_credentials request is granted.

      Starts from every resource-backed scope the authenticating endpoint registers for the named resource, the same set grantedResources(IuOidcClientEndpoint, URI, Set) computes for the authorization code flow. openid is not excluded specially, but nothing ever issues an ID token for it: this grant acts for the client itself, with no end user to claim one for, and a token endpoint only ever adds one alongside a redeemed grant.

      A scope parameter narrows that set to what it names rather than rejecting the request when it asks for less than everything registered; RFC 6749 §5.1 allows answering with a narrower scope than requested, so long as the response says what was actually granted.

      Parameters:
      endpoint - endpoint that authenticated
      issuer - this provider's issuer identifier
      scope - scope parameter value, or null to grant everything the resource registers
      resources - resource parameter values; empty if the request named none
      Returns:
      granted scopes
      See Also:
      • RFC 6749 §5.1
